title: Texas Ranks Among Worst States for Employee Burnout - NewsBreak
text:
By Billy Jenkins ,
18 hours ago
( KNUE-FM ) Texas is known of lots of different things, one of the most common is that Texans work extremely hard. course, there are exceptions to every rule, but for the most part, people in Texas don’t mind working hard to make sure they can provide for their family.
As of late the only way to survive is to work hard, just providing for our family has been more difficult but we have to take a break at some point, or we will get burnt out.
Which is why it’s not exactly shocking to find that Texas ranks as one of the worst states in the country when it comes to employee burnout .
Why Texas Ranks High for Burnout While it’s a good thing to know that people work hard, you need to take care of yourself too. When you ask your friends in neighbors in Texas what they have been up to lately, it’s almost always just working.
Texans are proud to make a living even if it means putting in long days. But remember, you have life smacking you in the face after you’re done with your workday, there is nothing wrong with taking some time for yourself.

READ MORE : The Most Stolen Items from Walmart Stores
How the Burnout Rankings Were Calculated These rankings were created by Wealth of Geeks and they made these rankings by state after looking at a few key metrics. Those metrics include income, quit rates, commute duration, working hours, safety, and paid time off.
Almost every year I lose PTO hours that I have accrued at work. It’s nobody’s fault but my own. But my plan is to take time off earlier in the year so I don’t have so much to burn at the end. Use your PTO, you’ve earned it!
Download the KNUE Mobile App Now The Worst States for Employee Burnout in 2025 Here are the states that have employees on the brink of burn out.
15 States Ranking Worst for Employee Burnout After long work days employees begin to get burnt out. Here is a list of states ranking worst for employee burnout. Gallery Credit: Billy Jenkins Canva 15. Michigan Michigan has some pretty bad work policies which correlates with their unhappy worker's score. Canva 14. Tennessee Tennessee is not known for being inclusive in the workplace. Which leads to a high employee dissatisfaction score. Canva 13. Idaho Idaho is bad when it comes to childcare policies in the workplace. Which leads to poor working conditions for women. Canva 12. Kentucky Kentucky has a high burn out score because resident find it difficult to find a good income that comes with job security. Canva 11. Delaware Delaware was high on this list as employees complain about a lack of flexibility from employers. Many would like to see more work from home options become available. Canva 10. New Mexico Employees in New Mexico have a hard time finding a good paying job. Other complaints include poor management and legal protection. Canva 9. New Jersey The biggest complaint from employees in New Jersey is being able to find a job where they are paid well. Canva 8. Virginia Virginia has a low employee satisfaction rate largely due to the states difficultly in providing unemployment insurance. Canva 7. Alabama Alabama employees are not happy with a few aspects such as low inclusiveness and poor health reform in the workplace. Canva 6. Pennsylvania The biggest struggle in Pennsylvania when it comes to employees is the high unemployment rates. Canva 5. South Carolina South Carolina has a high quit rate for employees partly due to a low annual income rate. Canva 4. New York New York has high employee burn out because of long commute times; employers also don't do a great job with employee safety policies. Canva 3. Florida Florida employers aren't great at providing PTO, work weeks are also mostly longer than 40 hours per week. Canva 2. Texas Workplace safety is a big problem which leads to unhappy employees. We also have the second longest work week average at over 43 hours per week. Canva 1. Georgia Commute times in Georgia are much worse than most believe. Georgia also has the highest rate of employees quitting. Burn out is real! 10 Most Dangerous Jobs We all work hard for a living, but some jobs are more dangerous than others, here is a look at the 10 most dangerous jobs. Gallery Credit: Billy Jenkins Canva 1. Truck Driver Just imagine driving a gigantic truck with a majority of people texting or looking at their phone next to you at high speeds. It's a recipe for disaster. So, THANK YOU truck drivers. Canva 2. Logging Workers Logging workers have lots of accidents often related to mediocre training procedures. Operating heavy machinery isn't easy. Canva 3. Roofers Many roofers have fallen off a roof at some point. Replacing or fixing roofs can be very dangerous which is why it's so important to follow safety protocols. Canva 4. Construction Workers Construction workers are often working in dangerous conditions. There are so many variables that could increase their chance of an accident. Canva 5. Farmers Farmers are surrounded by chemicals and heavy farm equipment. Both of which can lead to serious injury if a mistake is made. Canva 6. Underground Miners Doing any job underground always has a potential for serious danger. Especially when you add lack of training and supervision. Canva 7. Garbage Collection Moving at a quick speed, working with heavy equipment, and dangerous materials could all lead to workplace injuries. Canva 8. Steel Workers Creating fixtures to hold buildings together is going to put you in some dangerous situations. Working with steel is a difficult job. Canva 9. Pilot Especially with a pilot shortage, these individuals are working long hours and have to keep hundreds of people safe. This can be very stressful. Canva 10. Hunting and Fishing Many hunters and anglers are working with dangerous equipment where safety has to be priority number one. Defective machinery also leads to lots of injuries.
